title: Patch: the game log renders only the lines near the view
thread:
**Issue #4614 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4614: Patch: the game log renders only the lines near the view
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The list of what happened this game, the sidebar on a desktop and the popover behind the log toggle on a phone, draws every line of the whole game at once. In a long match that list grows into the hundreds of lines, and each new event lays the whole list out again, exactly while the phone is already busy animating the board. After this change the list draws only the lines around the part being read, about a screenful plus a safety margin, and holds the rest's place with blank space, so scrolling still reaches every line but the device only ever pays for the visible ones. A player in a forty-turn game on a phone feels the log open at once and the board stay smooth as new lines arrive. Nothing about what the log says, keeps, or offers changes.

## Why

- The log keeps the whole game now, not just the last stretch of events, so a long match accumulates hundreds of kept and window lines, capped at 1000 by the named constant in `apps/web/src/game/config.ts` (`LOG_HISTORY_LIMIT`). `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` maps every one of them to a `LogItem`, each carrying its own inspect hook and rich-text spans, with no windowing.
- Every new event also sets `scrollTop = scrollHeight` over that full list (`Log.tsx`), forcing the page to lay out all rows at the busiest moment; the deferred render softens it but the node count stays.
- The repository already solved this shape twice: the deck builder's pool (`apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/poolWindow.ts`, `usePoolWindow.ts`, #2334) and the collection Cards tab (`apps/web/src/collection/CardGrid.tsx`, #3734) mount only the rows near the viewport with an overscan margin, and the almanac list is virtual too. The game log is the remaining long list without it.
- It is none of the earlier log ideas under another name: #4561 was filtering by side and card (rejected), #1040 was scroll retention plus card links, #1692 was an unread badge on the phone toggle. This changes how many rows mount, not what the log holds or offers.

## Proposal

- Window the log's ordered list: mount the rows in and near the viewport with an overscan margin and keep the unmounted head and tail as sized spacers, so the scrollbar and every line's place stay the whole log's. Follow the pool's pattern: re-measure on scroll and resize, and draw everything where there is no layout to read (tests).
- Log lines vary in height (wrapped rich text, turn dividers), unlike the pool's uniform rows, so use per-row estimates corrected on measure rather than the pool's fixed pitch; do not bend the pool's grid arithmetic to fit.
- Keep today's behavior exactly: the newest line stays in view, the phone popover scrolls to the newest on open (`revealed`), turn dividers still draw, card lines still open their inspect overlay, and the always-mounted live announcer still speaks only the newest line. Presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7): no rule, view, or wording changes.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` (the windowing; keeps the deferred render, the memoised items and the announcer)
- A small list-window hook next to `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/usePoolWindow.ts`, or local to `apps/web/src/game/`, reusing the pool's approach without touching its grid arithmetic
- `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` and co-located tests for the hook
- SPEC section: §10.10 (the event feed the log draws). No spec change and no ruling: this makes no rules decision, it only draws the same lines cheaper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A log holding on the order of 1000 lines mounts only on the order of the viewport plus overscan rows in a real layout; a test with a mocked layout asserts the mounted row count stays bounded as the line count grows tenfold.
- [ ] Arriving lines still keep the newest line in view on desktop and in the phone popover on open; no scroll-retention or unread-badge behavior is added (those are #1040's and #1692's ideas, not this one).
- [ ] Turn dividers still render between turns, a line about a card still opens that card, and the live region still announces only the newest line.
- [ ] Hidden information is unchanged: unmounted lines mount with the same precomputed faces as today (R97 redaction untouched; unmounted rows leak nothing and show nothing early).
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Log.test.tsx` and the new hook tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` and the web lint stay clean with no new suppressions.

## Size and risks

- Size: medium. One component change, one small hook, tests; a few hundred lines in `apps/web` only.
- Risks: variable row heights make the spacer math fiddly (estimate, then correct on measure); new lines arriving while windowed must extend the tail spacer and re-pin the bottom without jitter; a row unmounted while its inspect sheet is open must close the sheet or stay mounted, following `CardGrid`'s precedent of keeping the interacted row mounted. Mitigate with a row-count assertion test rather than a timing test, since timings flake on shared runners.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45231104871)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Window the game log (`apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`) so it mounts only the rows in and near the viewport plus an overscan margin, holding the unmounted head and tail as sized spacers. A ~1000-line log mounts on the order of the viewport plus overscan rows. Everything the log says, keeps, and offers stays identical: newest line pinned in view, phone popover scrolling to newest on `revealed`, turn dividers, card inspect lines, the always-mounted live announcer speaking only the newest line, and R97 redaction untouched. No spec change and no ruling: this is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/config.ts` | change | Three named constants (rule 9): `LOG_OVERSCAN_ROWS`, `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX`, `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX` |
| `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.ts` | new | Pure arithmetic plus layout readers: `LogWindow`, `logWindow`, `logSpacers`, `sameLogWindow`, `fitLogWindow`, `readLogViewport` |
| `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.ts` | new | Hook returning the mounted index range, `"all"`, or `null`; scroll/resize/`ResizeObserver` wiring; per-row measurement |
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` | change | Wire the hook; head/tail spacer `li`s; first-mounted-row `value`; held-row tracking; bottom re-pin; keep deferred render, memoised items, history, announcer |
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | `.log--virtual` and `.log-spacer` classes only |
| `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts` | new | Arithmetic tests for `logWindow`/`logSpacers` |
| `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx` | new | Hook tests with mocked layout reads |
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` | change | New windowing suite; existing suites untouched |

Do not touch: `crates/*`, `spec/` (no note, no ruling, no pending paragraph), the pool files (`deckbuilder/poolWindow.ts`, `usePoolWindow.ts`, `PoolGrid.tsx`), `Board.tsx`, or anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: §10.10 (event feed, R745 history); no new ruling since no rules decision is made.

## Steps

1. **`config.ts`: add three constants** beside `LOG_HISTORY_LIMIT`, each with a one-line comment citing #4614: `LOG_OVERSCAN_ROWS = 10` (mounted rows past each viewport edge; rows not viewport-multiples, since row heights vary — rejected `POOL_OVERSCAN`-style multiples as the wrong unit); `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX = 24` (unmeasured-row estimate, corrected on measure); `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX = 8` (how close to the bottom counts as pinned).
2. **`logWindow.ts` (new): pure arithmetic, no DOM writes.** Types: `LogWindow = { first: number; last: number }`. `logWindow(count, heightAt: (index: number) => number, scrollTop: number, viewport: number, overscanRows: number): LogWindow` — walk cumulative offsets from `heightAt` (measured height or the estimate), find the visible range, extend by `overscanRows` rows each side, clamp to `[0, count-1]`. `logSpacers(count, heightAt, window): { head: number; tail: number }` — summed heights before `first` and after `last`. `sameLogWindow` / `fitLogWindow` (copy `sameWindow`/`fitWindow` from `poolWindow.ts`). `readLogViewport(list: HTMLElement): { scrollTop: number; clientHeight: number } | null` — return `null` when `clientHeight === 0` (no layout, e.g. jsdom), so callers draw everything, mirroring `readShape` returning `null`. Row heights are read by the hook (step 3), not here. Nothing here touches the pool's grid arithmetic.
3. **`useLogWindow.ts` (new): copy the shape of `usePoolWindow.ts`.** Signature: `useLogWindow(ref: RefObject<HTMLOListElement | null>, keys: readonly string[], heldKey: string | null): LogWindow | "all" | null`. State `view` starts `null` (mount everything on first render, as the pool does with `POOL_FIRST_CARDS`-equivalent full draw — here just all rows, since 1000 plain rows paint once cheaply). `measure(reshape)` reads `readLogViewport`; on `null` sets `"all"`. Otherwise builds `heightAt` from a `Map<key, height>` ref (missing keys use `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX`) plus the divider allowance below, and returns `fitLogWindow(logWindow(...))` with the held key's index unioned in (held always mounted, the `CardGrid` precedent). Listeners: the list's own `scroll` (the `ol` is the scroller) plus document-capture scroll (popover ancestors), window `resize` with `flushSync` (copy the pool), and a `ResizeObserver` on the list. Per-row measurement: a layout effect queries `li[data-log-key]` in the list, records `getBoundingClientRect().height` into the map (adding the matching `li[data-log-divider]` height for turn-divider rows), observes each row with the same observer, and re-measures when `keys` change. Return `"all"` handling identical to the pool.
4. **`Log.tsx`: wire the window around the existing `shown` array.** Compute `shown` exactly as today. Derive `keys = shown.map(line => line.key)`. Track `heldKey: string | null` with `onFocus`/`onBlur` on the `ol` (copy `CardGrid`: focus sets from `event.target.closest("[data-log-key]")`, blur clears when focus leaves the list) so a row with an open inspect sheet or focus stays mounted; rejected alternative was unmounting it, which would drop focus and close the sheet. `const window = useLogWindow(listRef, keys, heldKey)`; mount indices `first..last` when windowed, all rows when `null`/`"all"`. Render order inside the `ol`: head spacer `li`, mounted rows, tail spacer `li`. Spacers: `<li className="log-spacer" aria-hidden="true" style={{ height: N }} />` with `display: block` (the existing `.log-divider` precedent, which keeps them out of the `decimal` numbering). First mounted row's `LogItem` `li` gets `value={wholeIndex + 1}` so visible numbers keep whole-log numbering; dividers keep their current sibling-`li` form but gain `data-log-divider={line.key}`, and `LogItem`'s `li` gains `data-log-key={line.key}` plus an optional `value` prop. Keep `useDeferredValue`, the memoised `lines`/`faces`, `useLogHistory`, and the announcer reading `shown`'s newest (not the mounted slice). Pinning: keep the existing `useLayoutEffect` on `[view.events, revealed]`; add a `pinnedRef` set in the scroll handler (`scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight <= LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX`) and a layout effect on the window that re-pins (`scrollTop = scrollHeight`) only when pinned, so arrivals extend the tail spacer without jitter. No scroll-retention or unread-badge behavior is added (#1040/#1692 stay out).
5. **`board.css`: add two rules near `.log-divider`**: `.log--virtual` (no layout change; marker class for tests) and `.log-spacer { display: block; list-style: none; padding: 0; border: 0; }`. No other styling changes.
6. **Write `logWindow.test.ts`** (mirror `poolWindow.test.ts` style): mounted range plus overscan and no others; spacers sum to total height; unmeasured rows use the estimate; clamping past both edges; tenfold line count keeps mounted count bounded (e.g. same viewport over 100 vs 1000 rows mounts within a small constant factor — a row-count assertion, not timing).
7. **Write `useLogWindow.test.tsx`** (mirror `PoolGrid.virtual.test.tsx`: `vi.mock("./logWindow.ts")` for `readLogViewport`, driving bands by hand): `"all"` with no layout; scroll moves the window; held key stays mounted past the window and drops after blur.
8. **Extend `Log.test.tsx`** with a windowing suite that mocks `./logWindow.ts` reads (same `vi.mock` pattern): ~1000 kept lines (build history with the existing `advanceLogHistory` loop idiom) mount a bounded row count (assert `<= 60` `.log-line`s); a rerender with new events keeps `scrollTop === scrollHeight`; dividers still render before each turn's first line but the log's first; a card line still opens its sheet (copy the click test); the live region speaks only the newest line; far lines' text is absent from `innerHTML` (nothing leaks early). With the mock off, all lines draw (existing suites cover this; leave them unmodified).

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts` — "mounts the rows around the view plus overscan and no others"; "head and tail spacers sum to the whole height"; "unmeasured rows use the estimate until measured"; "clamps to the first row above and the last row below"; "tenfold lines keep the mounted count bounded".
- `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx` — "returns all where the page has no layout"; "moves the window on scroll and leaves the rest unmounted"; "keeps the held row mounted past the window, and drops it after blur".
- `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` (windowing suite) — "windows about 1000 lines to a bounded row count with a mocked layout"; "a new arrival keeps the newest line in view"; "dividers still draw before each turn's first line but the log's first"; "a card line still opens its inspect sheet"; "the live region still speaks only the newest line"; "unmounted lines render nothing".
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/logWindow.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Log.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx apps/web/src/game/logWindow.ts apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.ts apps/web/src/game/config.ts apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx`, plus `cargo fmt --check`.

## Done when

- [ ] A ~1000-line log with a mocked layout mounts on the order of viewport-plus-overscan rows, bounded as line count grows tenfold.
- [ ] New arrivals keep the newest line in view on desktop and on phone-popover open; no scroll-retention or unread-badge behavior added.
- [ ] Turn dividers, card inspect lines, and newest-only live announcements behave exactly as today.
- [ ] Unmounted lines render nothing and all faces stay precomputed (R97 unchanged; no hidden-information change).
- [ ] The three web test files, typecheck, eslint with no new suppressions, and `cargo fmt --check` are all green.

## Risks

- Variable row heights make spacer math fiddly: estimates plus per-row `ResizeObserver` correction contain the error, and spacers only affect blank space, never words. A wrong estimate degrades to slightly-off scroll position, not wrong content.
- New lines arriving while windowed could jitter the bottom: the pinned-only re-pin (within `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX`) means a user scrolled up is never yanked down.
- Decimal numbering could shift when rows unmount: spacers use `display: block` (the divider precedent, out of numbering) and the first mounted row pins its number with `value`, so visible numbers match today's.
- Determinism/replay: untouched — no engine, view, or wording code changes; `shown` is computed exactly as today and only the mounted slice differs.

## Open questions

None. Every choice above is the builder's to implement as specified; the rejected alternatives are recorded in the steps.
```

## Goal

Window the game log (`apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`) so it mounts only the rows in and near the viewport plus an overscan margin, holding the unmounted head and tail as sized spacers. A ~1000-line log mounts on the order of the viewport plus overscan rows. Everything the log says, keeps, and offers stays identical: newest line pinned in view, phone popover scrolling to newest on `revealed`, turn dividers, card inspect lines, the always-mounted live announcer speaking only the newest line, and R97 redaction untouched. No spec change and no ruling: this is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/config.ts` | change | Three named constants (rule 9): `LOG_OVERSCAN_ROWS`, `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX`, `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX` |
| `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.ts` | new | Pure arithmetic plus layout readers: `LogWindow`, `logWindow`, `logSpacers`, `sameLogWindow`, `fitLogWindow`, `readLogViewport` |
| `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.ts` | new | Hook returning the mounted index range, `"all"`, or `null`; scroll/resize/`ResizeObserver` wiring; per-row measurement |
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` | change | Wire the hook; head/tail spacer `li`s; first-mounted-row `value`; held-row tracking; bottom re-pin; keep deferred render, memoised items, history, announcer |
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | `.log--virtual` and `.log-spacer` classes only |
| `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts` | new | Arithmetic tests for `logWindow`/`logSpacers` |
| `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx` | new | Hook tests with mocked layout reads |
| `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` | change | New windowing suite; existing suites untouched |

Do not touch: `crates/*`, `spec/` (no note, no ruling, no pending paragraph), the pool files (`deckbuilder/poolWindow.ts`, `usePoolWindow.ts`, `PoolGrid.tsx`), `Board.tsx`, or anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: §10.10 (event feed, R745 history); no new ruling since no rules decision is made.

## Steps

1. **`config.ts`: add three constants** beside `LOG_HISTORY_LIMIT`, each with a one-line comment citing #4614: `LOG_OVERSCAN_ROWS = 10` (mounted rows past each viewport edge; rows not viewport-multiples, since row heights vary — rejected `POOL_OVERSCAN`-style multiples as the wrong unit); `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX = 24` (unmeasured-row estimate, corrected on measure); `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX = 8` (how close to the bottom counts as pinned).
2. **`logWindow.ts` (new): pure arithmetic, no DOM writes.** Types: `LogWindow = { first: number; last: number }`. `logWindow(count, heightAt: (index: number) => number, scrollTop: number, viewport: number, overscanRows: number): LogWindow` — walk cumulative offsets from `heightAt` (measured height or the estimate), find the visible range, extend by `overscanRows` rows each side, clamp to `[0, count-1]`. `logSpacers(count, heightAt, window): { head: number; tail: number }` — summed heights before `first` and after `last`. `sameLogWindow` / `fitLogWindow` (copy `sameWindow`/`fitWindow` from `poolWindow.ts`). `readLogViewport(list: HTMLElement): { scrollTop: number; clientHeight: number } | null` — return `null` when `clientHeight === 0` (no layout, e.g. jsdom), so callers draw everything, mirroring `readShape` returning `null`. Row heights are read by the hook (step 3), not here. Nothing here touches the pool's grid arithmetic.
3. **`useLogWindow.ts` (new): copy the shape of `usePoolWindow.ts`.** Signature: `useLogWindow(ref: RefObject<HTMLOListElement | null>, keys: readonly string[], heldKey: string | null): LogWindow | "all" | null`. State `view` starts `null` (mount everything on first render, as the pool does with `POOL_FIRST_CARDS`-equivalent full draw — here just all rows, since 1000 plain rows paint once cheaply). `measure(reshape)` reads `readLogViewport`; on `null` sets `"all"`. Otherwise builds `heightAt` from a `Map<key, height>` ref (missing keys use `LOG_ROW_ESTIMATE_PX`) plus the divider allowance below, and returns `fitLogWindow(logWindow(...))` with the held key's index unioned in (held always mounted, the `CardGrid` precedent). Listeners: the list's own `scroll` (the `ol` is the scroller) plus document-capture scroll (popover ancestors), window `resize` with `flushSync` (copy the pool), and a `ResizeObserver` on the list. Per-row measurement: a layout effect queries `li[data-log-key]` in the list, records `getBoundingClientRect().height` into the map (adding the matching `li[data-log-divider]` height for turn-divider rows), observes each row with the same observer, and re-measures when `keys` change. Return `"all"` handling identical to the pool.
4. **`Log.tsx`: wire the window around the existing `shown` array.** Compute `shown` exactly as today. Derive `keys = shown.map(line => line.key)`. Track `heldKey: string | null` with `onFocus`/`onBlur` on the `ol` (copy `CardGrid`: focus sets from `event.target.closest("[data-log-key]")`, blur clears when focus leaves the list) so a row with an open inspect sheet or focus stays mounted; rejected alternative was unmounting it, which would drop focus and close the sheet. `const window = useLogWindow(listRef, keys, heldKey)`; mount indices `first..last` when windowed, all rows when `null`/`"all"`. Render order inside the `ol`: head spacer `li`, mounted rows, tail spacer `li`. Spacers: `<li className="log-spacer" aria-hidden="true" style={{ height: N }} />` with `display: block` (the existing `.log-divider` precedent, which keeps them out of the `decimal` numbering). First mounted row's `LogItem` `li` gets `value={wholeIndex + 1}` so visible numbers keep whole-log numbering; dividers keep their current sibling-`li` form but gain `data-log-divider={line.key}`, and `LogItem`'s `li` gains `data-log-key={line.key}` plus an optional `value` prop. Keep `useDeferredValue`, the memoised `lines`/`faces`, `useLogHistory`, and the announcer reading `shown`'s newest (not the mounted slice). Pinning: keep the existing `useLayoutEffect` on `[view.events, revealed]`; add a `pinnedRef` set in the scroll handler (`scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight <= LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX`) and a layout effect on the window that re-pins (`scrollTop = scrollHeight`) only when pinned, so arrivals extend the tail spacer without jitter. No scroll-retention or unread-badge behavior is added (#1040/#1692 stay out).
5. **`board.css`: add two rules near `.log-divider`**: `.log--virtual` (no layout change; marker class for tests) and `.log-spacer { display: block; list-style: none; padding: 0; border: 0; }`. No other styling changes.
6. **Write `logWindow.test.ts`** (mirror `poolWindow.test.ts` style): mounted range plus overscan and no others; spacers sum to total height; unmeasured rows use the estimate; clamping past both edges; tenfold line count keeps mounted count bounded (e.g. same viewport over 100 vs 1000 rows mounts within a small constant factor — a row-count assertion, not timing).
7. **Write `useLogWindow.test.tsx`** (mirror `PoolGrid.virtual.test.tsx`: `vi.mock("./logWindow.ts")` for `readLogViewport`, driving bands by hand): `"all"` with no layout; scroll moves the window; held key stays mounted past the window and drops after blur.
8. **Extend `Log.test.tsx`** with a windowing suite that mocks `./logWindow.ts` reads (same `vi.mock` pattern): ~1000 kept lines (build history with the existing `advanceLogHistory` loop idiom) mount a bounded row count (assert `<= 60` `.log-line`s); a rerender with new events keeps `scrollTop === scrollHeight`; dividers still render before each turn's first line but the log's first; a card line still opens its sheet (copy the click test); the live region speaks only the newest line; far lines' text is absent from `innerHTML` (nothing leaks early). With the mock off, all lines draw (existing suites cover this; leave them unmodified).

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts` — "mounts the rows around the view plus overscan and no others"; "head and tail spacers sum to the whole height"; "unmeasured rows use the estimate until measured"; "clamps to the first row above and the last row below"; "tenfold lines keep the mounted count bounded".
- `apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx` — "returns all where the page has no layout"; "moves the window on scroll and leaves the rest unmounted"; "keeps the held row mounted past the window, and drops it after blur".
- `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` (windowing suite) — "windows about 1000 lines to a bounded row count with a mocked layout"; "a new arrival keeps the newest line in view"; "dividers still draw before each turn's first line but the log's first"; "a card line still opens its inspect sheet"; "the live region still speaks only the newest line"; "unmounted lines render nothing".
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/logWindow.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Log.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx apps/web/src/game/logWindow.ts apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.ts apps/web/src/game/config.ts apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx apps/web/src/game/logWindow.test.ts apps/web/src/game/useLogWindow.test.tsx`, plus `cargo fmt --check`.

## Done when

- [ ] A ~1000-line log with a mocked layout mounts on the order of viewport-plus-overscan rows, bounded as line count grows tenfold.
- [ ] New arrivals keep the newest line in view on desktop and on phone-popover open; no scroll-retention or unread-badge behavior added.
- [ ] Turn dividers, card inspect lines, and newest-only live announcements behave exactly as today.
- [ ] Unmounted lines render nothing and all faces stay precomputed (R97 unchanged; no hidden-information change).
- [ ] The three web test files, typecheck, eslint with no new suppressions, and `cargo fmt --check` are all green.

## Risks

- Variable row heights make spacer math fiddly: estimates plus per-row `ResizeObserver` correction contain the error, and spacers only affect blank space, never words. A wrong estimate degrades to slightly-off scroll position, not wrong content.
- New lines arriving while windowed could jitter the bottom: the pinned-only re-pin (within `LOG_PIN_TOLERANCE_PX`) means a user scrolled up is never yanked down.
- Decimal numbering could shift when rows unmount: spacers use `display: block` (the divider precedent, out of numbering) and the first mounted row pins its number with `value`, so visible numbers match today's.
- Determinism/replay: untouched — no engine, view, or wording code changes; `shown` is computed exactly as today and only the mounted slice differs.

## Open questions

None. Every choice above is the builder's to implement as specified; the rejected alternatives are recorded in the steps.
